pm_exper_user_3719_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) If you love homemade jam, try simmering a batch of strawberry or blueberry jam this weekend—the sweet, fruity aroma will drift through your home. You could also make a spiced apple butter for a warm, autumnal scent. Even a quick cranberry compote will make the kitchen smell incredible.
(b) If you want your home to smell amazing, try baking something simple like a fruit pie or a batch of cookies this weekend. You could also simmer a pot of spiced cider for a warm, inviting aroma. Even roasting vegetables with herbs can make the whole place feel cozy.
(c) If you love brewing artisan coffee, try roasting your own beans this weekend—the rich, toasty aroma will spread wonderfully through the house. You could also make a batch of cold brew concentrate for an all-day coffeehouse scent. A stovetop mocha syrup is another fragrant treat to prepare.
(d) If you love fresh-baked bread, try a no-knead artisan loaf or a simple focaccia this weekend—they’re low effort but fill the whole house with that irresistible bakery aroma. You could also bake cinnamon rolls on Sunday morning for an extra cozy scent. A quick batch of homemade garlic knots is another crowd-pleaser that smells amazing while baking.

**Southeast Asia:**  
- **Thai Tom Kha Gai** – A coconut milk–based soup with galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves. It can be made with only a hint of chili or none at all, letting the citrusy and herbal profile shine.
- **Malaysian Ayam Percik (mild version)** – Grilled chicken marinated in turmeric, lemongrass, and coconut milk glaze, with just gentle warmth from spices rather than pronounced heat.
- **Vietnamese Goi Cuon (Fresh Spring Rolls)** – Rice paper rolls filled with herbs, vegetables, and shrimp or pork, served with a sweet-savory peanut or hoisin-based dipping sauce instead of chili.

**Brazil:**  
- **Moqueca Baiana (mild version)** – A seafood stew with coconut milk, dendê oil, bell peppers, onions, and cilantro; the chili level can be kept very low without losing character.
- **Vatapá** – A creamy dish made with bread, shrimp, coconut milk, peanuts, and palm oil — rich and flavorful without requiring high heat.
- **Salpicão** – A colorful chicken salad with carrots, apples, raisins, and mayo-mustard dressing for a tangy, sweet-savory balance.

Later, the streets awaken with processions of saffron and white, and stalls serve fragrant bowls of plant-based noodle soup, coconut curries, and crispy fried bananas — dishes I savor for this one special week each year.
